summary.one_liner: A framework that lets multimodal AI models view a computer screen and operate it with mouse and keyboard actions to complete a user's objective.
summary.what_it_does: The framework gives a multimodal model the same screen-view inputs and mouse/keyboard outputs a human operator would use, so the model can look at the screen and decide on a sequence of actions to reach a stated objective. It is run from a terminal with the `operate` command, and the model is chosen with the `-m` flag. Supported models named in the README include GPT-4o (the default), GPT-4.1, o1, Gemini Pro Vision, Claude 3, Qwen-VL and LLaVA (via Ollama). Optional modes add OCR-based element lookup (`gpt-4-with-ocr`, described as the default for the project), Set-of-Mark prompting with a bundled YOLOv8 button-detection model (`gpt-4-with-som`), and voice input for the objective (`--voice`). The README says it was released in November 2023 and was one of the first examples of full computer use.
use_cases: automate repetitive tasks on a desktop computer
experiment with vision-capable LLMs controlling a GUI
compare multimodal models at computer operation
run a local multimodal model for screen control via Ollama
how_to_run: ollama pull llava && ollama serve && operate -m llava
notable: Runs one objective across many interchangeable vision models selected with a single -m flag
Set-of-Mark prompting mode with a bundled YOLOv8 button-detection weights file
OCR mode maps clickable text to screen coordinates so the model clicks by element text
Optional voice input for objectives, installed through a separate requirements file
Local model option through Ollama for LLaVA
caveats: The README says LLaVA error rates are very high and it is meant only as a base to build on
Ollama supports only macOS and Linux per the README, with Windows in preview
Using the default gpt-4o model requires an OpenAI account that has spent at least $5 in API credits
Mac users must grant Terminal Screen Recording and Accessibility permissions
